transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-04
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (Redwood CSM); Asha Patel (CTO, Helio), Liam O'Connor (Staff ML Engineer), Sara Gomez (SRE)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on observability readiness and fallback/rollback coordination for the pilot go/no-go. Reviewed latest telemetry (latency P50/P95, token costs), clarified canary thresholds, discussed automated fallback to smaller model variant and region failover, agreed on runbook edits and spike test. Action items assigned.

Topics:
- Canary definitions and metrics (latency, errors, traffic percentages)
- Fallback model variants and automatic routing policies
- Telemetry gaps: KV cache hit metrics, token-level cost breakdowns
- Runbook triggers and rollback criteria
- Pricing for dedicated burst capacity and how it affects SLOs

Action items (also captured above): see list

Transcript (timestamps rough, transcription imperfect in places):
[00:00:03] Jordan: All right folks, thanks for joining — let's try to keep to 45 minutes, big agenda today is observability and the fallback playbook.
[00:00:10] Asha: Yep, thanks Jordan. We really want a clear yes/no for go-live next week, so this is critical.
[00:00:15] Priya: Quick note, I uploaded a new draft of the canary runbook into the shared folder, it's labeled pilot-runbook-v2.pdf. It has the thresholds we discussed last week but I tweaked the error-rate windows.
[00:00:26] Liam: I saw that, thanks. One ask up front, can we add KV cache hit-rate as a top-level bullet? We saw big variance in the last sim where cold starts killed P95.
[00:00:35] Priya: Absolutely, Liam. We had the KV cache metric as 'optional' before, I'll bump to primary. To be clear, that metric is sometimes showing up in Redwood telemetry as K-V cash which is cute but we fixed naming in the last export.
[00:00:49] Sara: quick thing — when you say "fallback", is that auto-switch to a smaller model or fallback to a different region? We need to know the latency delta.
[00:00:58] Jordan: Good question. Our recommended policy is layered: primary fallback is model variant (e.g., from redwood-large-16q to redwood-medium-8q), then region fallback if capacity constrained. Priya, did you bring the latency delta numbers?
[00:01:10] Priya: I did. On our test bench for the sequences typical to Helio, the medium variant added ~14-20ms to P50 and ~60-140ms to P95, depending on sequence length. There's also a ~5% quality regression on edge cases — we documented the eval examples in the deck.
[00:01:27] Asha: The quality delta matters for customer-facing summaries; we need guardrails. If the fallback increases hallucination risk, it's not acceptable unless the degradation is only for non-critical endpoints.
[00:01:37] Marcus: Noted. We should tie fallback policies to endpoint-level risk classification — e.g., critical summaries always stay on primary or fail closed.
[00:01:44] Liam: Agreed. Also, what are the exact triggers? Error rate above X for Y minutes? P95 > Z for some time? We need concrete numeric thresholds.
[00:01:53] Priya: Proposed thresholds in the runbook:
- P95 latency > 1.2x baseline for 5 min -> start canary rollback evaluation
- Error rate > 1% (client-facing 4xx/5xx combined) for 3 min -> trigger canary to 1% traffic remaining and then fallback if persists
- KV cache miss rate increase by 15% over baseline for 10 min -> investigate and consider model warmup strategies
(there's a table in the doc with baseline values)
[00:02:26] Sara: That feels reasonable but can we add absolute thresholds not just multipliers? For SLO alerts our ops pager wants absolute numbers for initial triage.
[00:02:34] Priya: For sure — I'll add absolute P95 ms numbers and error counts in the next revision.
[00:02:40] Jordan: On the canary rollout itself, recommended slow ramp: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% over 4 hours, with checks at each stage. The team had suggested a faster 2-hour ramp — what's Helio's appetite?
[00:02:52] Asha: We prefer conservative given customer sensitivity; the 4-hour plan is okay, but we want to be able to abort quickly and route the small % to the old variant.
[00:03:01] Priya: Abort will route traffic back to the pinned model and then slash to 0% for the canary. That requires the traffic steering integration with your gateway — Sara, are you comfortable with that rollback path?
[00:03:11] Sara: We're good, we've done similar canary cancellation flows. We do want a playbook step that lists who hits the kill switch and who notifies customers.
[00:03:19] Marcus: We can own the customer notification template. Add that as an action item.
[00:03:23] Liam: One of the things we saw in the last run was token cost spikes during retries. Do you have token-level cost traces we can correlate to retries?
[00:03:31] Priya: Yes, Redwood telemetry has token-level breakdowns per API key and route; in the UI it's under 'Cost by Token'. We will export per-request traces for the sim. Note sometimes model names get fuzzy in system transcribes — e.g., redwood-dedicated got transcribed as 'redwood dedicate' in earlier exports.
[00:03:52] Asha: Haha the transcription is trying.
[00:03:55] Jordan: On dedicated burst pricing — quick reminder — if you commit to a reserved pool we can guarantee lower token latency and burst headroom. I'll send a sample commitment table later today.
[00:04:05] Asha: Do you have sample numbers? We need to evaluate cost vs SLA.
[00:04:09] Jordan: Yes, I'll provide a short matrix: baseline hosted price, dedicated reserved incremental price for burst, and sample SLA language.
[00:04:17] Sara: On telemetry gaps — one missing piece is detailed KV cache hit by user segment. We need to know if certain customer segments have worse cold cache behavior. Can Redwood export per-tenant KV stats?
[00:04:29] Priya: We can. We'll surface per-route and per-API-key KvCacheHitRate in the telemetry export. For private deployments there's an agent-based exporter, for hosted we provide the CSV export.
[00:04:41] Liam: For the spike sim, we want to simulate 3x traffic for peak 2 hours, with 20% synthetic degraded network to test regional failover. Does Redwood support region failover in the canary?
[00:04:53] Priya: Region failover is supported but it's a separate policy; in the runbook we recommend model variant fallback first, then region failover as a last resort because of latency and consistency. Region failover has a higher user-visible latency delta.
[00:05:06] Asha: What's the expected latency delta if we failover to EU region from us-west?
[00:05:10] Priya: From us-west to EU it's roughly +80-120ms on P95 in our telemetry for similar models — plus any additional queuing. We'll add exact numbers to the document.
[00:05:18] Marcus: Also, we recommend synthetic probing (small requests) every 30s to detect service-level degradation earlier than real traffic. That should be in the runbook steps.
[00:05:27] Sara: OK please add synthetic probes and who watches the alerts.
[00:05:31] Jordan: Let's talk about rollback criteria. Priya, you proposed both automated and manual rollback gates?
[00:05:37] Priya: Yes. Automated rollback: immediate and automatic for large error spikes (error rate > 3% sustained for 2 min) — system will cut canary to 0. Manual rollback: if P95 > absolute threshold or customer quality regressions flagged, SE will evaluate and then execute rollback with CSM + SRE sign-off.
[00:05:55] Liam: Who's signature is required to perform manual rollback? In my org we require SRE + Product.
[00:06:00] Marcus: Our proposed signoff: SRE + Helio responsible PM or CSM. For initial pilot we can accept SRE + CSM. We'll capture names in the runbook.
[00:06:09] Asha: Fine. We also need postmortem requirements — if there's an abort we want a 48-hour RCA with mitigation plan.
[00:06:15] Jordan: Sounds fair. We'll add a postmortem template in the runbook.
[00:06:20] Priya: Small nit — we noticed during the last sim that model warmup reduced the first 5 requests latency but didn't change steady-state. We propose a short warmup step during each rollout stage (10-20 requests per model node) to mitigate cold cache.
[00:06:33] Sara: Warmup is OK but make sure it's not expensive. We'll limit warmup to non-customer-visible requests.
[00:06:39] Liam: On the subject of telemetry retention, how long can we keep detailed traces for the pilot? We might need 30 days to debug intermittents.
[00:06:47] Priya: By default hosted telemetry retention is 14 days for full traces, 90 days for aggregated metrics. We can enable extended retention for pilot (30 days) — that's an add-on. I'll include the opt-in details.
[00:06:59] Asha: We'll opt in for 30 days for now.
[00:07:03] Jordan: Anything on compliance or security for cutover? Remember Helio is concerned about PII in prompts. We offer optional prompt redaction hooks and customer-managed KMS in Private.
[00:07:14] Asha: For the pilot we want logs redacted and KMS for any artifacts. Is that doable on hosted?
[00:07:19] Priya: On hosted we can enable prompt redaction and store artifacts in a redacted form. For customer-managed KMS that's part of Private or Dedicated with specific options; we'll outline tradeoffs in the security note.
[00:07:30] Sara: Good. Also, we need audit trail for who executed rollbacks. Does Redwood log that?
[00:07:34] Marcus: Yes audit logs are part of the Console. We'll ensure the runbook references the audit log location and include a sample query.
[00:07:42] Liam: Back to tests: timing — when can we run the 48h spike sim? Aim for next Tuesday?
[00:07:47] Asha: Tuesday works. Marcus, can you coordinate?
[00:07:50] Marcus: Yes I'll coordinate with Sara and provide a test plan.
[00:07:54] Jordan: Cool. Let's capture next steps quickly — Priya will update runbook with absolute numbers, KV cache promoted, synthetic probes, and warmup steps; Sara will run the sim and send telemetry; Jordan will send pricing and SLA.
[00:08:08] Asha: One last question — if the canary passes, what's the plan for full cutover? Is it a timed ramp across routes or a hard switch?
[00:08:15] Priya: Recommended full cutover is a staged ramp: keep traffic-steering rules and incrementally move route groups over 24 hours with automated checks every 30 min. Hard switch is only for emergency cases.
[00:08:27] Liam: How do we coordinate customer communications?
[00:08:29] Marcus: We will provide a communication template for pre-cutover and post-cutover notes and who sends them.
[00:08:35] Sara: Please add a sticky note in the runbook about maintenance windows.
[00:08:38] Priya: Will do.
[00:08:41] Jordan: All right I'm going to recap after a quick pause —
[00:08:45] [brief silence]
[00:08:48] Jordan: Recap: Priya update runbook (abs thresholds, KV cache promoted, warmup, synthetic probes); Sara run spike sim and send KV + token traces; Marcus coordinate test window Tuesday; Jordan provide pricing and SLA; Asha & team will review results and decide go/no-go. Agreed?
[00:09:05] Asha: Agreed.
[00:09:06] Liam: Agreed.
[00:09:07] Sara: Agreed.
[00:09:08] Priya: Agreed, I'll share PR tomorrow with the runbook diff.
[00:09:12] Jordan: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in Slack and Marcus will capture the schedule.
[00:09:18] Asha: Thanks all.

Notes on transcription: some names and model variants may be mis-transcribed in the raw export (e.g., 'redwood-medium' as 'red wood medium'). Where possible we've corrected them in the runbook link.

References shared in the call:
- pilot-runbook-v2.pdf (runbook draft)
- cost-latency-matrix.xlsx (pricing sketch)
- sim-instructions.md (load script and delta network config)

End of transcript.
